solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: British old school painter

explanation.surface: Describes some traditional British artist trained in a conventional academy.
explanation.walkthrough: Hieronymus Bosch was Dutch, so 'British old school' misleads as a description rather than three abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was a Netherlandish artist famous for his nightmarish visionary panels.

clue.text: Violent blow following blunder (by 1 across, as the saying goes?)

definitions.meaning: a hard, heavy strike, as in a punch

definitions.text: following blunder (by 1 across, as the saying goes?)
definitions.meaning: the British catchphrase 'bish ... bosh' (job done, easily) puts this word after 'bish', slang for a blunder, and before 'bosh', which sounds like the painter at 1 across

explanation.surface: A hard punch comes after a mistake, followed by a proverbial phrase about a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bish bash bosh' is a British expression meaning something done quickly and easily; 'bish' is also schoolboy slang for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard hit or wallop is commonly called this in informal English.

clue.text: Allowed in using "bish bosh" — the group passwords

indicators.note: the word for permitted is placed inside the reworked letters
the letters of bish bosh are put to use in a new order, a loose signal to rearrange them

parts.note: allowed means let, as in let someone pass

explanation.surface: A gang admits members who utter the jokey phrase 'bish bosh' as their secret code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using' is a loose rearrangement signal; the reworked letters are split after six to take in the word for permitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Words or customs used to identify members of a group and exclude outsiders, like a test word at a checkpoint.

clue.text: Drop-out seen in fast-food joints

parts.note: a hip is a joint of the body
a pie is a quick snack food

explanation.surface: A student who has quit is spotted in burger bars.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts appear in the clue in reverse order but join with the joint first; 'fast-food joints' looks like one phrase for restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the 1960s counterculture was often seen as someone who had dropped out of conventional society.

clue.text: Grouped together, making lots of noise between the sheets!

indicators.note: the noise word sits between the parts of the word for where sheets go

parts.note: the sheets suggests a bed
a racket is a loud din

explanation.surface: A couple makes a great deal of noise in bed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Items set within brackets are classed or linked together as a unit.

clue.text: Playing rugby, dad wears nothing for protection

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wear, that is surround, the zero
playing suggests the letters are in motion and rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A father plays rugby naked, without any padding.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside BDYGUARD, the rearrangement of RUGBYDAD, after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal guard is someone hired to shield a person from harm, a source of security.

clue.text: They're against 8; one who prays?

indicators.note: the entry at 8 down means to cut off the head, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: the praying mantis is an insect named for its posture

explanation.surface: Opponents of beheading are equated with someone at prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' stands for the answer at 8 down, an instruction to behead; 'one who prays?' is the insect, with the question mark flagging the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: People opposed to something are informally called by this plural of the prefix meaning 'against'.

clue.text: Partially developed blurred photograph enrages Sheik

indicators.note: a blurred image has its parts jumbled, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A fuzzy, half-developed picture annoys an Arab chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partially developed' looks like a description of the photograph, but it is the definition: very small or young.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase describes a child who is still very small, not yet grown up.

clue.text: See 6
Top secret (a tip ace detective comes up with)

indicators.note: comes up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the phrase comes with the letters inside it, carrying them across word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A top-secret tip from a great sleuth emerges.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'comes up' signals reading upwards; the parenthesis makes it look like an aside about a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is slang for killing them, and beheading is one way to do it.

clue.text: It guards quiet flat with fashionable interior

indicators.note: the trendy word goes inside, in the interior

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a pad is slang for a flat or home
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Describes a silent apartment with a stylish inside, oddly framed as a guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer wears a protective plate on the lower leg to shield it from kicks.

clue.text: Chap enters, to be announced in charge of ancient Egyptian city

indicators.note: the man word goes into the abbreviation

parts.note: a chap is a he

explanation.surface: A man arrives to be presented as governor of an old Egyptian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to Thebes, the ancient capital of Upper Egypt.

clue.text: Provides filler for tricky game; St. Helens' first appearance on back page

parts.note: bridge is a card game built on tricks
ST is the abbreviation for Saint

indicators.note: the first letter of Helens' is taken
back means the word for a sheet is read backwards

explanation.surface: Reads like a sports report: something fills a gap, and St Helens, a rugby league club, debuts on the back page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky game' means a game of tricks, i.e. bridge; 'appearance on' is link material. St Helens is a town in north-west England with a famous rugby league side.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill an empty space between two things is to connect across the divide.

clue.text: See 6
Bleak winter hasn't started to trouble little 'un

indicators.note: troubled letters are stirred up and rearranged
the opening letter of winter is dropped

explanation.surface: A harsh winter begins to bother a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: BLEAK plus INTER (winter without its W) is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A small child is jokingly called this because toddlers are at ankle height.

clue.text: Infielder regularly carries 10 water

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A baseball fielder carries some water.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'Infielder'. '10' refers to the answer at 10 across, the city adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes stood on the banks of this great river, so it is the water of that city.

clue.text: Made one's mark, reportedly, in skin transplant

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are said aloud

parts.note: signed one's name, as a celebrity does

explanation.surface: Someone signed during a skin graft procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A graft of tissue taken from the patient's own body is the medical term here.

clue.text: Call for heads, possibly, to roll with trouble in store

parts.note: to roll a die or coin is to throw or flip it
if you are 'for it' you are about to get into trouble

explanation.surface: Someone invites beheadings in a riot, with problems lurking in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' is not decapitation but one side of a coin; 'to' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Flipping a coin to decide is settled by someone choosing heads or tails.

clue.text: Well-built, wearing spectacles, Penny was easy to spot

indicators.note: the stout word wears, or encloses, the other letters

parts.note: stout means sturdy, well-built
OO looks like a pair of glasses
D is the old British abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A sturdy woman named Penny in glasses was conspicuous.
explanation.walkthrough: D is from the Latin denarius, the pre-1971 British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Being conspicuous means being prominent or noticeable among others.

clue.text: Left oddly situated? These will help you find your bearings

definitions.text: These will help you find your bearings

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in a strange place gets help to orient themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of angular distance north or south of the equator help in navigation and locating position.

clue.text: Knock back teaspoonful of sulphur? I say!

indicators.note: to knock back is to swallow, here read as turning the letters backwards
a teaspoon full of sulphur puts the element inside the spoon abbreviation

parts.note: TSP is the abbreviation for teaspoon
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Someone downs a spoonful of sulphur and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' looks like drinking but signals reversal of TSSP.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations to attract someone's attention quietly.

clue.text: This month's record ball striker

parts.note: INST, for instant, is an old business abbreviation for this month
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A footballer's monthly record for kicking.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched upper part of the foot is used to strike a football.

clue.text: He'll give you the lowdown on British Airways' soundproof design

parts.note: BA is the airline's abbreviation; the possessive adds S

indicators.note: design means the letters are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: An airline's quiet cabin is explained in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowdown' is the deepest singing, not inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer with the deepest bass voice gives out the lowest notes.

clue.text: Part of the media, Bill's in the Olympic venue

indicators.note: the bill word goes inside the city

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympics
an ad, or advertisement, is a bill

explanation.surface: A poster is displayed at the Olympic site.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting by sound is one branch of the mass media.

clue.text: One much admired, Labour leader supports union agreement

indicators.note: in a down clue the leader letter sits below and supports the rest

parts.note: I do is said when agreeing to a marriage union

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter

explanation.surface: A popular figure, the Labour party's head, backs a trade union deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' is marriage, not a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A person greatly revered or worshipped is a hero or star.

clue.text: Purchase storage on ship heading eastbound

parts.note: heading east is going to E, the compass abbreviation
a ship's hold is its cargo space

explanation.surface: Buying cargo space on a vessel sailing east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' means grip, not buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a firm grip or foothold, a small space for gripping.

clue.text: It hit Prescott, ex-deputy PM, leaving Sri Lanka

indicators.note: the Sri Lanka code leaves, that is is removed from, the politician

parts.note: Nick Clegg was UK deputy prime minister 2010-15
CL is Sri Lanka's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: Recalls a missile that struck a former UK deputy prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott, Labour deputy PM, was famously struck by this on the 2001 campaign trail and punched the thrower. 'ex-deputy PM' is a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: The missile thrown at Prescott in 2001 was a chicken's ovum.

clue.text: Made manual key corrections in Jaguar E-type drivetrain

indicators.note: the letters are inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A mechanic adjusts by hand inside a classic Jaguar car's transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manual key' suggests a gearbox, but means typewriter keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyed text again on a keyboard to fix errors.

clue.text: Fought to oust unionist creating disturbance outside — it might kick off!

indicators.note: the disturbance word goes outside the rest

parts.note: a riot is a public disturbance

indicators.note: creating suggests the letters are made into something new
to oust is to throw out, so the unionist letter is expelled from the word

explanation.surface: A unionist is fought and removed, causing a riot, with violence looming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating' is the rearrangement signal on what remains of 'Fought'; the exclamation mark hints at a pun on a match kicking off.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer often starts the game by kicking with the dominant lower limb.

clue.text: High-level programming language has one in danger

indicators.note: the letter for one goes in the language name

parts.note: Perl is a high-level programming language
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A computer language contains a risky element.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril means serious risk or jeopardy.
